_meta.indication: Reducing elevated intraocular pressure in patients with open-angle glaucoma or ocular hypertension

pivotal_trials.phase: Phase III pivotal non-inferiority efficacy study
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-masked, parallel group, multicenter, 12-month trial comparing PC tafluprost 0.0015% with PC timolol 0.5%
pivotal_trials.population: Patients aged 18 years or older with open-angle glaucoma or ocular hypertension
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Protocol-specified primary outcome measure was the difference in diurnal IOP reduction at Month 6 from baseline
pivotal_trials.n: 458 patients randomized (267 to tafluprost, 191 to timolol)
pivotal_trials.result: Tafluprost reached the predetermined criterion for non-inferiority (1.5 mmHg) at each visit and time point versus timolol

pivotal_trials.phase: Phase III pivotal non-inferiority efficacy study
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, multicenter, active comparator-controlled, 12-week, double-masked trial comparing PF tafluprost 0.0015% with PF timolol 0.5%
pivotal_trials.population: Patients aged 18 years or older with open-angle glaucoma or ocular hypertension
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Protocol-specified primary outcome measure was mean IOP change from baseline at all 9 time points during the study
pivotal_trials.n: 643 patients randomized (320 to tafluprost, 323 to timolol)
pivotal_trials.result: IOP-lowering effect of PF tafluprost was within the 1.5 mmHg non-inferiority margin compared to PF timolol at all visits and time points

key_safety: Most common ocular adverse reaction was conjunctival hyperemia (range 4%–20%); ocular reactions ≥2% included ocular stinging/irritation (7%), ocular pruritus (5%), cataract (3%), dry eye (3%), ocular pain (3%); common nonocular reactions included headache (6%)
target_moa: Tafluprost acid, a prostaglandin analog, is a selective FP prostanoid receptor agonist believed to reduce intraocular pressure by increasing uveoscleral outflow
modality: small molecule (fluorinated prostaglandin F2α analog ester prodrug)

advisory_committee.vote: Not referred to an FDA advisory committee because it is a member of the class of ophthalmic prostaglandin analogs with similar potential risks and benefits as other members in this class

summary.text: ZIOPTAN (tafluprost) was submitted as a 505(b)(1) NDA under standard review for a new molecular entity; it received a Complete Response letter on November 7, 2011 for lack of adequate sterility assurance, and was approved after the January 13, 2012 resubmission addressed the deficiency, with no accelerated approval, orphan, breakthrough, or priority-review designations stated.

Date of Original Submission	January 7, 2011 (standard review)
Complete Response Letter	November 7, 2011
Resubmission	Jan
A *Complete Response* letter was issued November 7, 2011, because the application did not provide adequate assurance of sterility of the final drug product.

Based on the review of the January 13, 2012, resubmission of NDA 202514, the applicant has addressed the manufacturing deficiencies outlined in the *Complete Response* letter dated November 7, 2011, submitted a safety update and resubmitted labeling including a new statement in the package insert that the date when the foil package is opened should be written on the package. Therefore, I agree with the reviewers that the application should be issued an *Approval* letter.
